prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at the light when struck from behind by the third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Both drivers reported no immediate complaints at scene, though claimant later reported headache and dizziness.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to go through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and filed. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records for the past several years through counsel.

Entry 3: Claimant's medical records received. Diagnosis includes concussion with post-concussive symptoms, followed by a referral to neurology. Treating physician notes ongoing light-duty restrictions. Reviewing records for consistency with the reported mechanism of impact and any pre-existing conditions.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding status of the bodily injury evaluation. Attorney indicated the client is still undergoing treatment and requested that we hold off on any settlement discussion until treatment reaches maximum medical improvement. Advised that an independent medical examination may be scheduled, and counsel did not object in principle.

Entry 5: Independent medical exam scheduled through counsel's office. Adjuster to request a copy of the IME report on completion. Liability remains clear based on the police report and the insured's account. File reserves to be reviewed once the medical picture is more complete.
